Series derivative coverage¶

Where each differentiable Series op gets its reverse (and forward-mode) rule. Same split as the local PyTorch tree: a declarative src/CodeM/native/derivatives.yaml for elementwise primitives, hand-written nodes for the structural / indexing / reduction / linalg families, and transitive (composite) gradients for everything built out of those.

  • 28 declarative unary primitive rules

  • 7 declarative binary primitive rules

  • 99 ops with an explicit hand-written reverse node

  • 134 ops total with a dedicated derivative

  • everything else on the public surface is composite-transitive or non-differentiable; correctness is pinned by tests/CodeM/test_autodiff_sweep.cpp (finite-difference) and tests/CodeM/test_patch177_cpu_torch_autograd_parity.cpp (libtorch oracle)

This table is a static index parsed from the sources. The runtime- authoritative list of what actually forms a reverse node is the [autodiff-sweep] classification report; per-op libtorch parity lives in the oracle’s [generated] / [parity] cases. Regenerate this file with python3 tools/audit/gen_derivative_coverage.py after changing derivatives.yaml or a maybe_link_* call site.
